Job title:  Podiatrist 

  Job type:  Full time or part time 

  Salary offer:  $71k to $105k annually + super + CPD allowance + benefits 

  Location:  Brisbane 

   

  About the company:   

 Our client is a respected, Podiatrist-owned organisation operating within established multidisciplinary clinics. With a team of 16+ podiatrists already on board, they’ve built a reputation for excellence in  Biomechanics, Sports, Exercise, and Musculoskeletal Podiatry . 

   

  About the role:  

 As a Clinic-Based Podiatrist, you’ll deliver high-quality assessments and treatments across a diverse caseload of  musculoskeletal, paediatric, and general care  patients — roughly a 50/50 split between musculoskeletal and general care cases. 

 You’ll have the opportunity to: 

 
	 Build and manage your own patient list 
	 Work alongside Physiotherapists and other Allied Health professionals 
	 Contribute to a dynamic, supportive clinical environment 
	 Develop your expertise in  Sports, Exercise & Biomechanical Podiatry  
 

   

  Benefits:   

 
	  Attractive remuneration  
	  Annual $2,000 CPD allowance , plus  bonus and commission  opportunities 
	  Flexible full-time or part-time options  
	  Mentoring & support:  Weekly, fortnightly, or monthly sessions based on experience level 
	  Career pathways:  Leadership and clinical specialisation streams 
	  Employer-funded parental leave  
	  Work-life balance:  Choose your location – Brisbane, Sunshine Coast, or Gold Coast 
	  Professional development:  Monthly case studies, in-house CPD, and biannual workshops 
	  Wellbeing support:  Employee Assistance Program (EAP) 
	  Staff discounts  on the full suite of allied health services 
 

   

  Requirements:  

 
	 Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Podiatry 
	 Current  AHPRA registration  (or eligibility to obtain) 
	 Strong communication and teamwork skills 
	 Commitment to continuous professional growth and evidence-based practice 
	 Passion for helping patients achieve optimal health outcomes 
 

   

 Ready to find your Podiatry home and grow with the best?  APPLY NOW  to join a team where your work is valued, your growth is supported, and your passion is shared.   Apply Now

result.description: THE TRUSTEE FOR THE BABBLE TRUST   About the role   Reporting to the Head Chef, the Junior Sous Chef will assist in the day-to-day operation of the kitchen, ensuring consistently high food standards while supporting and mentoring junior team members. You will play an important role in maintaining quality, food safety and efficient kitchen operations.   Key responsibilities    Assist the Head Chef with the daily operation of the kitchen and service  Oversee preparation, cooking and presentation of dishes to Bistro Rex's quality and presentation standards  Ensure consistency across all menu items and daily specials  Assist with menu development and seasonal menu changes  Supervise, train and mentor junior chefs and kitchen staff  Ensure compliance with food safety, hygiene and HACCP procedures  Monitor stock levels, assist with ordering and stocktakes, and minimise waste  Maintain a clean, organised and efficient kitchen environment  Work collaboratively with the kitchen team to deliver exceptional service during busy periods    About you   To be successful in this role you will have:   A relevant qualification or at least three years' relevant experience in lieu of qualifications  At least one-two years' experience in a quality, high-volume restaurant kitchen  Previous experience supervising or mentoring junior kitchen staff  Strong knowledge of food preparation, cooking techniques and kitchen operations  Sound understanding of food safety, hygiene and HACCP principles  Excellent organisational and communication skills  A positive attitude with a willingness to learn and develop  Passion for quality produce and attention to detail  The ability to remain calm and perform under pressure      About Company    Bistro Rex is a busy, well-established French-inspired bistro in the heart of Potts Point, known for its commitment to exceptional produce and our nose-to-tail philosophy. We are seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Junior Sous Chef to join our passionate kitchen team. A busy medical centre in  Trinity Gardens  has a  part-time  opportunity for a  General Practitioner  to support its large patient base. This  mixed-billing  clinic is open seven days a week to provide comprehensive healthcare to the local community in a professional and supportive environment. 

 The centre features 12 consult rooms, a four-bed treatment room, and a separate procedure room. It is equipped with onsite allied health services, including pathology, podiatry, and physiotherapy, as well as a co-located skin cancer, cosmetic, and vein clinic. This provides a great opportunity for a GP to pursue special interests. The practice offers robust support, with full-time and CDM nurses dedicated to patient care and an experienced administrative team that helps build GP practices and supports individual billing choices to maximize earning potential. 

 This role offers flexible working arrangements and the clinical autonomy to shape your practice to your specific interests, especially in areas like skin, aesthetics, and occupational medicine. The practice is committed to professional growth, with resources that simplify RACGP CPD requirements and opportunities to become a GP Registrar Supervisor. Located just 5 kilometers from the Adelaide city center, Trinity Gardens offers a suburban lifestyle with easy access to city amenities, making it a convenient and desirable place to live and work. General Practitioner (GP) — Contract Opportunity Across Australia 

 Join a dynamic HealthTech startup and wellness centre delivering modern, patient-centred primary care through blended in-person and telehealth services. We are seeking experienced General Practitioners with full Australian registration and residency or citizenship to work on a contract basis across Australia. This role offers flexibility, strong professional support, and competitive billings-based pay of  65%–70% on billings . 

 What You’ll Do 

 
	 Provide high-quality general practice consultations to diverse adult and family populations via telehealth and in-clinic sessions. 
	 Deliver comprehensive assessments, diagnosis, management plans, acute care and chronic disease management in line with best practice guidelines. 
	 Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team including allied health, mental health clinicians, and digital health specialists to coordinate patient care. 
	 Use the HealthTech platform to document encounters, follow up results, prescribe and refer, and support continuity of care. 
	 Participate in targeted quality improvement projects, remote case reviews, and virtual clinical governance meetings. 
 

 Who You Are 

 
	 Registered with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) as a General Practitioner. 
	 Australian citizen or permanent resident eligible to work across Australian states and territories. 
	 Experienced in general practice or family medicine with strong clinical decision-making and communication skills. 
	 Comfortable with telehealth platforms and digital patient records, plus the ability to balance virtual and face-to-face consultations. 
	 Committed to delivering patient-centred, evidence-based care with cultural sensitivity and respect for diverse communities. 
 

 Why Join Us 

 
	  Flexible hours:  Design a schedule that fits your lifestyle, with options for part-time or concentrated clinic blocks. 
	  Professional development:  Training provided, access to clinical upskilling, peer review, and mentorship within a growing HealthTech practice. 
	  Attractive earnings:  Competitive percentage on billings between 65% and 70% with transparent revenue sharing. 
	  Innovative environment:  Work with cutting-edge digital tools, telehealth infrastructure, and a mission-driven team focused on accessible care. 
	  Nationwide opportunities:  Contract roles available across Australia, enabling a range of practice locations and patient communities. 
 

  Ideal Candidates  

 We welcome applications from: 

 
	 GP Registrars 
	 VR GPs 
	 Non-VR GPs 
	 Doctors with previous telehealth experience 
	 Doctors seeking flexible work-from-home arrangements 
 

 Start Timeframe and Contract Details 

 Positions begin from a fixed date with contract terms tailored to clinician preference and site needs. Personal Care Assistant (NDIS)

Employer: HI FIVE COMMUNITY SERVICES PTY LTD
Location: WERRIBEE, Victoria 
Salary: $80000 per annum + superannuation
Employment Type: Full-time
Job Type: Permanent (38 hours Full-time)

About the Role
At HI FIVE Community Services, we believe support should feel personal, not just professional. We’re a close-knit team that genuinely cares about the people we work with, and we’re committed to helping individuals living with disabilities live life on their own terms with dignity, choice, and independence.
For us, it’s not just about providing services; it’s about building real relationships. We take the time to understand each participant their goals, their routines, and what matters most to them. Whether it’s supporting everyday activities, building confidence, or encouraging community participation, we stand beside our participants every step of the way.
Our approach is simple: treat people with respect, show up with compassion, and do the little things that make a big difference. At HI FIVE, we aim to create a warm and supportive environment where participants feel valued and our team feels proud of the impact they make every day.
Because at the heart of what we do is one belief everyone deserves the opportunity to live a full and meaningful life.
Key Responsibilities
•	Provide assistance with personal care including showering, grooming, dressing, toileting, and mobility while maintaining dignity and individual preferences 
•	Support participants to develop independence and life skills in line with their NDIS goals and daily routines 
•	Assist with light domestic duties such as meal preparation, cleaning, laundry, and shopping to maintain a safe living environment 
•	Facilitate community access by accompanying or transporting participants to social, recreational, or educational activities 
•	Monitor participants’ wellbeing and report any changes or concerns to supervisors or relevant health professionals 
•	Maintain accurate records of care, progress, and incidents in accordance with organisational and NDIS requirements 
•	Assist with rehabilitation activities, therapeutic exercises, and basic treatments under the guidance of allied health professionals 
•	Provide support to therapists during sessions and assist with medication administration where trained and authorised 
•	Ensure compliance with NDIS Practice Standards, workplace health and safety, and mandatory reporting obligations


Skills and Experience Required
•	Certificate III or higher in Aged Care, Individual Support, or equivalent
•	Minimum 12 months’ relevant work experience required Australia/Overseas
•	Current First Aid and CPR certificate
•	National Police Check and Working with Children Check (or willingness to obtain)
•	Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
•	Ability to work independently and in a team
•	Empathy, patience, and a strong commitment to quality care

Desirable
•	Experience working with elderly clients or people with disabilities
•	Valid driver’s licence and access to a vehicle (for community care roles)
•	Multilingual abilities a plus
•	Ability to work various shifts including weekends and public holidays

What We Offer
•	Competitive salary and benefits
•	Supportive and inclusive team culture
•	Ongoing professional development and training
•	Opportunities for career advancement
•	Flexible working arrangements

How to Apply
Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter outlining your experience and suitability for the role.
